message: Job "docker" uses docker/build-push-action without cache-from and cache-to configuration.
why: Without layer caching, every CI run rebuilds all Docker layers from scratch, adding minutes per build. docker/build-push-action supports cache-from and cache-to natively; the simplest setup uses the GitHub Actions cache backend.
suggestion: Add cache-from and cache-to to the docker/build-push-action step. For example: `cache-from: type=gha` and `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max`. If this build also runs on pull requests, note GHA cache entries written there are readable only within that same PR and mode=max exports every stage: prefer `mode=min` on PR runs or keep the export for branch builds only, and keep mode=max for branch builds.
measurementHint: Compare Docker build wall-clock time before and after adding layer caching, including any export upload time on PR runs and eviction of branch-scoped entries. A multi-minute reduction is common for images with several layers.
aiHandoff: Review job "docker" in .github/workflows/docker.yml and add `cache-from: type=gha` and `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max` to the docker/build-push-action step unless `no-cache: true` is intentional. If the job also runs on pull requests, scope the export to branch builds or use mode=min there.

message: Job "docker" uses QEMU for ARM Docker builds targeting linux/arm64.
why: This job builds ARM Docker images through QEMU emulation for linux/arm64, which is often slower and less reliable than using a native arm64 runner for the same target.
suggestion: If this job primarily targets linux/arm64, consider a native arm64 runner instead of QEMU emulation.
measurementHint: Compare wall-clock build time, cache reuse, and failure rate between the current QEMU path and a native arm64 or split-platform build path.
aiHandoff: Review .github/workflows/docker.yml job "docker" and, if it mainly builds linux/arm64 through QEMU, test a native arm64 runner instead of emulation.

message: The workflow has no workflow-level or job-level concurrency setting.
why: Superseded read-only checks can waste runner time, but publication and deployment runs may need to finish and retain every queued release.
suggestion: Cancel superseded read-only PR/branch checks only, preferably at job level. Do not cancel release/publish/deploy work. For serialized publication consider cancel-in-progress: false with queue: max (up to 100 pending); this is not a lossless release queue or a dispatch-order guarantee.
measurementHint: For read-only checks, confirm superseded runs stop without canceling unrelated checks. For publication, verify in-progress completion, queued-release retention and required ordering under bursts.
aiHandoff: Review .github/workflows/docker.yml before adding concurrency. Isolate superseded read-only validation from publication/deployment, including opaque scripts and reusable workflows. Do not cancel publication or copy a latest-only CI group onto it. Default concurrency replaces pending runs even with cancel-in-progress: false; queue: max retains at most 100 pending and does not guarantee dispatch order. Use a durable queue if every release must run.
